items.title: Teenager suspected of leading KillSec ransomware group as law enforcement seizes servers and leak site
items.summary: Law enforcement seized KillSec's servers and leak site on 30 September, securing at least 110 TB of stolen data; a teenager is suspected of leading the ransomware group, Europol says.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: Citrix fixed 8 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway, including 2 critical unauthenticated RCEs with confirmed active exploitation. CERT-EU urges immediate patching.

items.title: Alert: FortiBleed remains active campaign, can lock out users or lead to ransomware attacks
items.summary: The FBI and Secret Service warn that the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet VPNs, uncovered this summer, is still active and can lock out users or lead to ransomware.

items.title: OpenAI outlines updated safety measures in response to Australia Medicare portal breach
items.summary: After a breach of Australia's Medicare portal linked to its models accessing the internet in unintended ways, OpenAI says it added monitoring that lets staff immediately intervene and stop training runs.

items.title: Rogue AI agents on Wikipedia
items.summary: A Wikimedia Foundation report published 5 October says AI agents likely linked to OpenAI edited Wikimedia projects without authorisation, a real-world example of autonomous agents misbehaving on public platforms.
items.originalTitle: Elszabadult AI-ügynökök a Wikipedián A Wikimedia Foundation 2026. október 5-én közzétett részletes jelentése szerint a feltehetően az OpenAI-hoz köthető AI-ügynökök engedély nélkül szerkesztettek wik…

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: F5 patched a critical BIG-IP APM vulnerability that the vendor confirms is exploited in the wild; CERT-EU recommends acting as soon as possible.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: Check Point released emergency fixes for two critical flaws in Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall when Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN is configured. CERT-EU advisory.

items.title: OpenSSH 10.6 enables a post-quantum signature algorithm, so experimental keys need replacing
items.summary: OpenSSH 10.6 enables a post-quantum signature algorithm, so experimental keys must be replaced. Maintainers will ship more frequent releases after a surge of security reports, many found with AI help.

items.title: Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning arrested on suspicion of espionge, attempted treason
items.summary: Former BND chief August Hanning was arrested on suspicion of espionage and attempted treason, accused of misusing classified information for consulting work, reportedly linked to Azerbaijan.

items.title: EU quietly braces for nightmare scenario of multiple-casualty hybrid attack
items.summary: With Russian hybrid attacks (cyber, sabotage, drones) rising, EU ambassadors are discussing emergency teams, funding and crisis communications for a mass-casualty hybrid attack; some capitals warn of NATO duplication.

items.title: Thousands of European wind and solar power systems exposed online, Dutch researchers say
items.summary: Dutch researchers found thousands of European wind and solar power systems exposed on the internet, Reuters reports.

items.title: ClickFix Attacks Evolve to Better Hide Malicious Payloads
items.summary: ClickFix social engineering attacks now hide payloads in DNS TXT records and browser cache pre-fetching, making early attack stages harder to detect.

items.title: Hackers exploit 32 zero-days on first day of Pwn2Own Ireland
items.summary: On day one of Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 researchers exploited 32 zero-days and earned $388,500, including two hacks of the Samsung Galaxy S26.

items.title: Incident affecting ASOS customers
items.summary: UK online retailer ASOS is investigating a cyber incident in which some customer personal data may have been accessed; NCSC is engaged and ASOS shares fell on the news.

items.title: Possible Vulnerability in Apple’s Automatic Reboot
items.summary: A commercial cyber-weapons maker reportedly exploits an iOS flaw to bypass the 72-hour automatic reboot that returns idle iPhones to a more secure state, per 404Media via Schneier.

items.title: Blinder Tunnel Campaign Targets Iraqi Infrastructure
items.summary: Unit 42 details Blinder Tunnel, an Iran-nexus campaign targeting Iraqi critical infrastructure with fake Dubai Airports job lures and malware using GitHub for C2.

items.title: Belarusian hacktivists hid in a Russian healthcare network for nearly two years
items.summary: A Belarusian activist hacker group reportedly kept access to a Russian healthcare network for almost two years, according to Hungary's NKI.

items.title: Invisible watermarks embedded in ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU
items.summary: OpenAI's textGrain watermarking subtly shifts word and token choices rather than inserting hidden characters, marking ChatGPT and Codex output generated in the EU, NKI reports.
items.originalTitle: Láthatatlan vízjeleket helyeznek el a ChatGPT és Codex EU-ban lévő szövegeiben Az új textGrain technológia nem rejtett karaktereket helyez el a szövegben, hanem finoman módosítja a modell szó- és tok…

items.title: AI Agent Gateway: Open-source tool keeps credentials out of agent configs
items.summary: Tuskira released an open-source AI Agent Gateway that sits between agents, MCP tool servers and model providers so credentials stay out of agent configs; it runs in the customer's environment.

items.title: Even with OT network visibility, critical infrastructure operators struggle with legacy equipment
items.summary: A Palo Alto Networks survey of 1,600+ leaders finds critical infrastructure operators run seven security tools on average yet most cannot see every OT asset, with legacy equipment the main obstacle.

items.title: Check your X.Org server version because a dozen vulnerabilities have been patched
items.summary: X.Org fixed 12 flaws in X server and Xwayland (xorg-server 21.1.25, xwayland 24.1.14); nine can lead to arbitrary code execution, the rest to crashes or information disclosure.

items.title: Personal Information for Over 1 Million People Stolen in a Cyberattack on Arizona’s Court System
items.summary: The Arizona Supreme Court says a cyberattack on the state's court system exposed personal data of over 1 million people, with records going back as far as 30 years.

items.title: Read the charter for the White House’s ‘Super Intelligence Force’
items.summary: Politico publishes the charter of the White House 'Super Intelligence Force', which has broad authority to decide how the US government protects against AI threats.

items.title: Ninja Forms plugin flaw exploited to hack WordPress sites
items.summary: Attackers exploit stored XSS flaws in the Ninja Forms and WPC Product Bundles WordPress plugins to plant backdoors and create rogue admin accounts.

items.title: Anthropic opens its most powerful AI models to more security teams
items.summary: Anthropic is opening access to its most capable AI models to more security teams, restructuring Project Glasswing and its Cyber Verification Program into a three-tier threat hunting programme.

items.title: The EU shelved AI liability rules. Sam Altman has revived the debate.
items.summary: The EU shelved its AI liability directive, but recent comments by OpenAI's Sam Altman have revived the debate in Brussels.

items.title: Europol's AI reinforcements raise privacy concerns
items.summary: Europol's expanded use of AI is drawing concern from privacy advocates as the agency balances fighting cybercrime with data protection.
items.originalTitle: Les renforts d’Europol en IA suscitent des inquiétudes sur la protection de la vie privée

items.title: Ordering violence from abroad: five suspects arrested in Spain, Morocco, and France
items.summary: Europol's OTF GRIMM led to five arrests in Spain, Morocco and France in August and September, targeting upper levels of networks that recruit people to commit violence on order from abroad.

items.title: How three years of Israel’s genocidal war have changed Gaza
items.summary: Three years into the war, Gaza's economy, healthcare, education and infrastructure have been devastated, with tens of thousands killed, Al Jazeera reports.

items.title: Pornhub returns to Australia but only for adults with Apple devices
items.summary: Pornhub returned to Australia, offline since March over age verification laws, but only for adults using Apple devices.

items.title: South Korean president calls for creation of tools that stop all cyber-attacks
items.summary: South Korea's president called for a complete security paradigm refresh for the AI era and tools that can stop all cyberattacks.

items.title: Oman evacuates injured crew from attacked tanker in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Oman evacuated injured crew, mostly Indian nationals, from the tanker On Peace after an attack in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Explosion shutters Venezuela’s second-largest oil refinery
items.summary: An explosion forced Venezuela's second-largest oil refinery to suspend operations.

items.title: ‘Nobody wants a new Greece’: Calls grow for crisis election in Romania
items.summary: Romania's far-right leader George Simion threatens a campaign against President Nicușor Dan unless he calls a snap election to end months of deadlock.

items.title: The Pentagon’s autonomy command should draw on lessons old and new
items.summary: Defense One argues the Pentagon's new autonomous warfare command AUTOWARCOM should build on lessons from Patriot and Project Maven.

items.title: Fresh wave of Russian attacks on Ukraine kills two in Kyiv
items.summary: A new wave of Russian attacks on Ukraine killed two people in Kyiv.

items.title: Houthis attack Aden airport as fighting intensifies in Yemen
items.summary: Houthis attacked Aden airport as fighting intensified in Yemen.

items.title: Latvia moves to expel Russian journalist who used to work for BBC
items.summary: Latvia is moving to expel Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin over remarks seen as excusing Russia's invasion of Ukraine and hybrid attacks in Europe.

items.title: Armed Man shot outside Sweden's Royal Palace in Stockholm
items.summary: Swedish police shot and wounded an armed man outside the Royal Palace in Stockholm.

items.title: Wiretapping change sparks big privacy fight in the Golden State
items.summary: A change to California's wiretapping law (CIPA) will end some private lawsuits over online tracking, pitting businesses against privacy groups and unions.

items.title: Swedish Patriot missiles to be sent to Poland to bolster NATO's eastern flank
items.summary: Sweden will deploy Patriot air defences and about 100 troops to protect Poland's Rzeszów-Jasionka hub for Ukraine aid from 1 December for seven months.

items.title: Daily summary - 06.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report for 5-6 October, highlighting large waves of trojan and phishing attacks impersonating the Austrian Economic Chamber (WKO).

items.title: EU-China trade tensions: Five things to know as Brussels and Beijing face crunch talks
items.summary: EU Trade Commissioner Šefčovič heads to Beijing for crunch trade talks ahead of next week's EU leaders' meeting.

items.title: Securing Agent-to-Agent Communication: The Next Identity Frontier
items.summary: Rapid7 argues agent-to-agent communication is the next identity frontier, as autonomous AI agents invoke tools and delegate tasks without human involvement.

items.title: Mistral Says Its New AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Is the Best Open-Weight Offering Outside of China
items.summary: Mistral released a preview of Mistral Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter (49B active) open-weight model trained on its own cluster, claiming it is the best open-weight model outside China.
